label: Core Concepts
desc: 30 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Benefits, Storage, Comparison and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: What is Parquet?

subs.label: Benefits
subs.desc: Key benefits include efficient compression, faster query performance, reduced storage costs, excellent schema evolution support, and compatibility with multiple data processing frameworks.

subs.label: Storage
subs.desc: Columnar storage stores data by columns instead of rows, allowing efficient compression and faster query performance when accessing specific columns.

subs.label: Comparison
subs.desc: How does Parquet compare to CSV? What is the difference between Parquet and ORC?

subs.label: File Structure
subs.desc: A Parquet file contains: magic bytes (header), one or more row groups, metadata, and a footer with schema and statistics information.

subs.label: Compression
subs.desc: Snappy is a fast compression algorithm that prioritizes speed over compression ratio, offering a good balance between compression and query performance.

subs.label: Schema
subs.desc: Parquet supports adding, removing, and reordering columns, allowing schema changes without rewriting entire files.

subs.label: Reading
subs.desc: How do you read Parquet files?

subs.label: Writing
subs.desc: How do you write Parquet files?

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: Partitioning dramatically improves performance by reducing the amount of data scanned — queries only read the relevant partitions.

subs.label: Statistics
subs.desc: Min-max statistics store the minimum and maximum values for each column chunk, enabling the query engine to skip row groups that can't match a filter condition.

subs.label: Data Quality
subs.desc: Missing values are represented as NULL and tracked in the file metadata, maintaining data integrity.

subs.label: Data Types
subs.desc: Parquet supports logical types that map to underlying physical types, allowing automatic conversion while maintaining data semantics.

subs.label: Nested Data
subs.desc: Yes, Parquet supports nested/complex types like arrays, maps, and structs through its record shredding and assembly algorithm.

subs.label: Spark
subs.desc: Spark uses Parquet as its default storage format, reading/writing DataFrames in Parquet with built-in optimizations and compression support.

subs.label: Data Lakes
subs.desc: Parquet is the standard format for data lakes because of its efficient storage, query performance, schema evolution support, and compatibility with a wide range of tools.

subs.label: Partitioning
subs.desc: How do you partition Parquet files?

subs.label: Optimization
subs.desc: How do you optimize Parquet file size?

subs.label: Encoding
subs.desc: Dictionary encoding replaces repeated values with dictionary indices, reducing file size for low-cardinality columns.

subs.label: Use Cases
subs.desc: What are common use cases for Parquet?
